title: K-Means
description: Centroid-based clustering algorithm partitioning data into K distinct clusters.
name: K-Means
summary: K-Means partitions N observations into K clusters in which each observation belongs to the cluster with the nearest mean (cluster centroid), acting as a prototype of the cluster.
use_when: Partitioning unlabeled numeric data into spherical clusters where K is known or easy to estimate.
avoid_when: Clusters have irregular shapes, varying densities, or are heavily dominated by outliers.
pros: Highly scalable to large datasets using mini-batch variations.
Conceptually simple and easy to implement and execute.
cons: Requires pre-specifying the exact number of clusters K.
Highly sensitive to initial centroid selection (mitigated by K-Means++).
Assumes spherical clusters of similar size and density.

key_hyperparams.name: n_clusters
key_hyperparams.note: The number of clusters to form as well as the number of centroids to generate.

quick_start:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 0], [10, 2], [10, 4], [10, 0]])
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0).fit(X)
labels = kmeans.labels_
